the 300 item version of the International Personality Inventory Pool NEO (IPIP-NEO) is a valid measure of the five-factor model, and the IRT based 120 item version (IPIP-120) has similar validity.
the IPIP NEO is a valid and reliable measure of the five factors of personality, and that it can be reduced to a 120 item measure that is equally valid and reliable.
the 300 item and 120 item IIP NEOs are reliable and valid measures of the Big Five and can be used in place of the NEO PI R for research purposes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of IPIP items to measure the five factor model of personality.
the development and testing of a 120-item IPIP NEO.
the development of a brief IPIP NEO measure that can be easily and freely administered and scored, and that has the potential to be used in a variety of contexts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IPIP 120 IRT based measure is a viable alternative to the 300 item version of the measure and that both versions are reliable and valid measures of the five factor structure.
the IPIP 300, IPIP 120 (Johnson) and IPIP 120 IRT based measures all demonstrate strong psychometric properties, and can be used as reliable, valid and cost-effective alternatives to the NEO PI.
the IPIP NEO is an accurate representation of the NEO PI R, and the two 120 item measures are reliable, valid, and efficient representations of the IPIP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 300 item and both 120 IPIP NEO measures are valid and useful measures of the five factor theory of personality.
the IPIP NEO is a valid and reliable instrument that can be used in place of the NEO PI R for the assessment of the five factor personality model.
the IPIP NEO, as well as both 120 item measures, can be used with confidence in research and applied settings as an alternative to the NEO PI.

the IPIP NEO, as well as its 120 item versions, can be used with confidence in both research and applied settings as a reliable and valid measure of the five-factor model of personality.
